svg.title: From Qualified File to Funded Commission
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-01-broker-deal-path; chapter number: 1; chart type: process_flow; title: From Qualified File to Funded Commission; subtitle: The five-step commercial broker path practitioners describe; caption: The broker lends no money, scores and packages the file, places it with the lender whose credit box fits, and is paid only when the deal funds.; assumptions note: Step order combines operator gates from separate speakers. The $30,000 figure is Shane Walton's worked example of a $2 million loan at 1.5 points.; note: Sources are John Neufer, CFM (Commercial Financing Mastery) with Sua Truong, and Shane Walton of the Commercial Loan Broker Institute.; stages: step: 01; label: Score the file before quoting points; value: Step 1; detail: Neufer weighs deal size, deal type, borrower constraints and time pressure, sets the hair clause up front, and targets $5,000 to $10,000 per deal.; step: 02; label: Confirm lender appetite this week; value: Step 2; detail: Truong calls bank commercial managers on Monday or Tuesday to ask where the money is going, because portfolios fill up by asset type.; step: 03; label: Take a packaging deposit; value: Step 3; detail: Walton takes a deposit as small as $250 with a 45-day LOI refund clause before the heavy lifting begins.; step: 04; label: Place with the lender that fits; value: Step 4; detail: Most clients are a best fit for just one, two or three lenders, so the file goes where the credit box matches.; step: 05; label: Collect points when the deal funds; value: Step 5; detail: Funded amount times points, with most products paying 1% to 6%. A $2 million loan at 1.5 points pays $30,000.
